ai.description: This snake reaches 30–40 cm. It is dark brown or purplish with a yellow-spotted belly and a distinct, shield-like, truncated tail tip. It belongs to the family Uropeltidae.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Uropeltis pulneyensis* is best distinguished by its unique, sharply truncated tail ending in a large, flat, circular or oval shield that is distinctly keeled or ridged.
ai.habitat: *Uropeltis pulneyensis* inhabits the high-altitude montane shola forests and grasslands of the Palni Hills in the Western Ghats, typically above 1,500 meters.
ai.behavior: *Uropeltis pulneyensis* is a fossorial snake that spends most of its life underground, emerging to the surface primarily during or after heavy monsoon rains.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Uropeltis pulneyensis* is viviparous, giving birth to a small litter of live young. Breeding typically occurs during the monsoon season, between June and August.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Uropeltis pulneyensis* is endemic to the high-elevation grasslands and shola forests of the Palani Hills in the Western Ghats, Tamil Nadu, at altitudes above 1,800 meters.
